column3: NASB follows the critical text; “was presenting a defense” is rendered “proceeded to make his defense.” A full-width colon appears in the NASB text.
NASB reorders the verse.
NASB follows the critical text without “you”; “acquainted” is rendered “an expert,” and “controversies” is “questions.”
NASB follows the critical text and reorders the verse; it adds “own.”
NASB renders “from the first” as “for a long time previously.”
NASB follows the critical text; “being judged” is rendered “standing trial.”
NASB follows the critical text without “Agrippa”; it adds “the promise” and “God” and reorders the verse.
NASB renders “by you” as “among you people” and adds “does.”
NASB renders “contrary” as “hostile.”
NASB follows the critical text; it adds “just,” “not only,” and “but also.”
NASB renders “was compelling” as “tried to force” and “was persecuting” as “kept pursuing.”
NASB follows the critical text; “during which” is rendered “While thus engaged.”
NASB reorders the verse and renders “above the brightness of the sun” as “brighter than the sun.”
NASB follows the critical text; “language” is rendered “dialect.”
NASB follows the critical text (“the Lord”).
NASB follows the critical text; “servant” is rendered “minister,” and it adds “not only … but also.”
NASB renders “the people” as “the Jewish people.”
NASB renders “power” as “dominion.” A stray quotation mark appears in the NASB text.
NASB renders “So then” as “Consequently” and “was not disobedient” as “did not prove disobedient.”
NASB follows the critical text; it renders “I was declaring” as “kept declaring” and adds “then” and “even.”
NASB follows the critical text without the article; it reads “some Jews.”
NASB follows the critical text; “bearing witness” is rendered “testifying.”
NASB renders “our people” as “the Jewish people” and adds “by reason of.” A stray quotation mark appears in the NASB text.
NASB follows the critical text; “You are insane” is rendered “you are out of your mind.”
NASB follows the critical text; it supplies “said” and renders “of truth and sobriety” as “of sober truth.”
NASB renders “hiding from him” as “escape his notice.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB follows the critical text, rendering it “In a short time you will persuade me”; the meaning is uncertain.
NASB follows the critical text (“in much”); “I would wish” is rendered “I would to God,” and “in much” is “long time.”
NASB follows the critical text without “And when he had said these things.”
